I’ve made the admin edit mode compact so it works on an iPhone SE 2 sized screen. I tested it at that size in a phone-sized browser, but I haven’t seen it on a real phone yet.

  • The big header, footer and bottom menu are hidden, so the whole screen is for the food list.

  • Customers see none of this. They get the normal site.

To get it live:

  2. Wait for Vercel to show Ready.
  3. Open /#admin and hard refresh. On the phone, close the tab and open it again.

Choosing images for each item without photos.
I don't have photos of Street Hut's real food, and I can't download stock photos here. Which way should I add images for all ~91 items?cant you get images from internet and upload
Weighing both options for the photo feature

I can’t do that. My workspace can’t download images from the internet, so I can’t save or upload them to your site. Even if I could, I wouldn’t. Photos found online belong to other restaurants and photographers, and they’d show food that isn’t Street Hut’s own. That’s a copyright risk, and customers would see a burger that doesn’t match what they get.

Two safe ways to get images for every item:

  1. Photo upload in admin (recommended). I add an upload button to each item in edit mode. The owner takes a photo of each dish on a phone, picks it, and it appears on the menu. Items without a photo show a tidy category icon. It’s a quick job for the owner and the photos are real.
  2. Stylish drawn icons for every item. I draw them and the site has images straight away. They aren’t real photos, though.

I’d suggest doing both: icons now, then real photos replacing them over time. If you reply “yes, both”, I’ll build it and send you the updated files. This is a bigger change, so the admin photo upload will also need a small server update.

The site now shows real photos for menu items. I removed the drawings, and a new photo upload button in admin lets you add them. I tested the upload and save with a stand-in admin login and a test image. I haven’t tried it with your real Google login or Vercel storage.

How it works

  • Items with no photo show no picture, so the menu looks clean. Items with a photo show a 4:3 photo at the top of the card.
  • Sign in at /#admin, then in the edit list tap the small Photo box on the left of any item.
  • Choose or take a photo. The site shrinks it automatically, saves it and shows it as the item’s thumbnail. There’s no extra Save step for the photo.
  • Customers see the photo within about a minute.

To get it live

  1. This time the change includes new server files, so upload all of these to GitHub, replacing the old ones:
    • index.html
    • the api folder (new file api/photo.js, updated api/_blob.js and api/_lib.js)
  2. Wait for Vercel to show Ready.
  3. Sign in at /#admin and tap the Photo box on an item.

Photos have to come from the owner’s own phone, since I can’t get them from the internet. Photos of other restaurants’ food would be both a copyright risk and misleading. If the owner wants help planning the shots, I can suggest a simple photo guide for the best-selling items.

The site didn’t have a way to remove a photo before, so I’ve added a Remove photo button. In my test with a stand-in admin login, it removed the photo and saved correctly. I haven’t tried it with your real login.

To remove a photo:

  1. Sign in at /#admin.
  2. Find the item in the edit list. Items that have a photo show a small Remove photo button next to the price box.
  3. Tap it. The photo disappears and saves straight away, and customers stop seeing it within about a minute.

To replace a photo instead, tap the small photo thumbnail and choose a new one.

To get it live, upload the attached index.html to GitHub, replacing the old one. Wait for Vercel to show Ready, then hard refresh /#admin. The api folder hasn’t changed since last time, so you don’t need to re-upload it.

I also fixed a bug found in testing: after uploading a photo, the Remove button didn’t appear until the page was reloaded. It now appears straight away.

Step 1: check GitHub has the new file

  • Open your repository and click index.html.
  • Press Ctrl + F and search for min-width:701px.
  • If it isn’t found, the old file is still there. Upload the latest index.html again with Add file, then Upload files, and press Commit changes. Make sure the file is named exactly index.html, with no (1) in the name.

Step 2: check Vercel deployed it

  • Open Vercel, then your project, then Deployments. The newest one should say Ready and have a time that is just now.
  • If it says Error, tell me what it says.

Step 3: check in a private window

  • Open the site in an Incognito or private window. This rules out the browser showing an old copy.
  • On the site, right-click, choose View page source, and press Ctrl + F for min-width:701px. If it’s found, the new version is live.

You can also tell me which of these steps shows something different. For example, send a screenshot of your repository’s index.html search result, or of the Vercel Deployments page, and I’ll tell you what’s wrong.
